tests/graph-threads.test.ts: after replaying 399.session at speed 0 into a seeded Graph (demo seed helper), threadFromSet('replay-399', 'Sunday as played') has 6 songs in the order Rico Suave Bossa Nova, Leroy's Latin Lament, Woman of the World, What's Going On, Coffy Is The Color, Glide (Woman of the World once); an unknown ref throws 'no set: <ref>'; a duplicate thread name throws
README 'Threads and graphs' CLI list gains the command; npm run check --silent is green

features.description: The design doc has a §13 'Two-way graph ↔ playlist sync' note stating what wins on conflict, as a design only.
steps: docs/specs/2026-10-14-threads-and-graphs-design.md gains §13 (under 60 lines): the one-way export of D24 restated; the conflict cases (song added on one side, removed on one side, reordered on both); a recommended rule (last writer wins per song membership, order from the side edited last, with a dry-run diff shown first) marked *default*; what the sync would need (playlist changed timestamp from getPlaylist, a graphs.synced_at column) and an explicit 'not built in this run'
OVERNIGHT.md 'Needs Michael' gains one line pointing at §13 with the question 'which side wins when both changed?'
No code changed; npm run check --silent is green
